subject: computing
subtitle: How operating systems manage hardware and resources, and the difference between system and application software.

data.targetWord: system software that manages all hardware resources and provides a platform for application software to run on

examples.en-GB: Windows 11 is an operating system that manages the CPU, RAM, and storage on a laptop.

data.targetWord: the core component of an operating system that has direct control over hardware and manages low-level system operations

examples.en-GB: The kernel allocates CPU time to each running process and manages access to RAM.

data.targetWord: the ability of an operating system to run multiple processes apparently simultaneously by rapidly switching CPU time between them

examples.en-GB: Multitasking allows you to listen to music, browse the web, and type a document at the same time.

data.targetWord: the OS function that allocates portions of RAM to each running program and ensures programs do not overwrite each other's data

examples.en-GB: Memory management ensures that your video editor and music app each get their own separate area of RAM.

data.targetWord: the means by which a user interacts with a computer, which may be graphical (GUI) or text-based (CLI)

examples.en-GB: The user interface on a smartphone uses touchscreen icons and menus rather than typed commands.

data.targetWord: Graphical User Interface — an interface using visual elements such as windows, icons, menus, and a pointer to allow users to interact with a computer

examples.en-GB: The GUI on Windows lets users drag files into folders by moving the mouse rather than typing commands.

data.targetWord: Command Line Interface — a text-based interface where the user types precise commands and the OS responds with text output

examples.en-GB: A server administrator uses a CLI to manage the web server by typing commands like ls and mkdir.

data.targetWord: Windows, Icons, Menus, Pointer — the four visual elements that make up a graphical user interface

examples.en-GB: WIMP describes how you interact with a desktop OS: clicking icons, opening menus, and dragging windows with a pointer.

data.targetWord: the OS function that organises, creates, reads, writes, and deletes files and folders on storage devices using a file system

examples.en-GB: File management keeps track of where every document is stored on the hard drive so you can find it by name.

data.targetWord: a small piece of software that acts as a translator between the operating system and a specific hardware device, allowing them to communicate

examples.en-GB: A printer driver translates print commands from the OS into the specific instructions that a particular printer model understands.

data.targetWord: software that manages and controls the hardware, providing the platform on which application software runs; includes the OS, drivers, and utilities

examples.en-GB: The operating system, device drivers, and antivirus software are all examples of system software.

data.targetWord: software designed to help users perform specific tasks such as word processing, web browsing, or playing games; runs on top of the OS

examples.en-GB: Microsoft Word, Google Chrome, and Spotify are all examples of application software.

data.targetWord: a sub-category of system software that performs maintenance, optimisation, and security tasks to keep the computer running smoothly

examples.en-GB: Antivirus software and disk defragmenters are utility software that maintain and protect the computer system.

data.targetWord: a program that is currently being executed by the CPU, including the program code and all data it is using at that moment

examples.en-GB: When you open a web browser, the OS creates a process for it and allocates CPU time and RAM to run it.

data.targetWord: a signal sent to the CPU by hardware or software indicating that an event needs immediate attention, causing the CPU to pause its current task

examples.en-GB: When you press a key, the keyboard sends an interrupt to the CPU so it can process your keystroke immediately.

data.targetWord: a technique where the OS uses part of the secondary storage (hard drive) as extra RAM when physical RAM is full, allowing more programs to run than RAM alone would permit

examples.en-GB: When all your RAM is used, virtual memory lets the OS move less-used data to the hard drive to free up space for active programs.

data.targetWord: software whose source code is publicly available for anyone to view, modify, and redistribute, often developed collaboratively by a community

examples.en-GB: Linux is open source software — anyone can read its code, suggest improvements, or create their own version.

data.targetWord: software whose source code is kept secret and owned by the developing company; users cannot view or modify it and usually must pay to use it

examples.en-GB: Microsoft Windows is proprietary software — only Microsoft employees can see and modify its source code.

data.targetWord: permanent software programmed directly into a hardware device's read-only memory that controls its basic functions

examples.en-GB: The firmware in a router controls how it routes network traffic, and is stored in the device's built-in memory.

data.targetWord: the OS hiding the complexity of hardware from application programs, so applications can work without knowing the specific details of each hardware device

examples.en-GB: Hardware abstraction means a word processor can print to any printer without needing to know that printer's specific communication protocol.

data.targetWord: the method the OS uses to organise, store, and track files on a storage device, using a hierarchical folder structure

examples.en-GB: NTFS is the file system used by Windows to organise files on a hard drive into folders and subfolders.

data.targetWord: the OS function that decides which process gets CPU time and for how long, enabling multiple processes to share the processor fairly

examples.en-GB: Process scheduling ensures the music player and web browser both get enough CPU time to run smoothly at the same time.

data.targetWord: utility software that reorganises fragmented files on a hard disk drive so that related data is stored together, improving read speed

examples.en-GB: Running the disk defragmenter after months of use can make a hard drive noticeably faster by reducing fragmentation.

data.targetWord: utility software that detects, blocks, and removes malicious software from a computer system

examples.en-GB: Antivirus software scans downloaded files and emails to detect and remove viruses before they can cause damage.

data.targetWord: utility software that automatically creates copies of files and stores them safely so data can be recovered if the originals are lost or damaged

examples.en-GB: Backup software copies your photos and documents to an external drive each night so nothing is lost if the main drive fails.

data.title: Put these steps in the correct order for what the OS does when a program is launched:
items: The user double-clicks the program icon or runs the program command
The OS creates a new process for the program
The OS allocates a block of RAM to the process
The OS loads the program code from storage into RAM
The OS scheduler gives the process CPU time to execute
The program begins running and its user interface appears on screen

data.title: Put these steps in the correct order for how the OS handles virtual memory when RAM is full:
items: All available physical RAM is used up by running processes
A new program is opened and requires additional memory
The OS identifies the least recently used data currently in RAM
The OS moves that data from RAM to a designated area of the hard drive (the swap file)
The freed RAM space is allocated to the new program
If the swapped-out data is needed again, the OS moves it back from the hard drive to RAM
